mcq.q: A 16-year-old is appointed as agent by an adult principal. Which is correct?
options: A minor can never be an agent
The agency is void, and the principal is not bound
The minor is personally liable to the principal for negligence
The minor can be an agent, but he is not responsible to the principal — Section 184
mcq.explain: Section 184: anyone can act as an agent so far as third parties and the principal's liability are concerned, but only an adult of sound mind can be held answerable to the principal. The principal is bound by the minor agent's acts; the minor is not liable to the principal.
mcq.fast: Minor CAN be an agent (principal bound), but cannot be made liable to the principal.

mcq.q: Under Section 185, consideration for creating an agency is:
options: Necessary and must be in money
Not necessary
Necessary only for a general agent
Necessary if the agency is in writing
mcq.explain: Section 185 states that no consideration is necessary to create an agency. A friend who agrees to sell your goods without any commission is still your agent, with all the duties of an agent. Payment or remuneration affects his rights to commission, not the existence of the agency.

mcq.q: Which statement about ratification is NOT correct?
options: Ratification may be express or implied
The whole transaction must be ratified, not just part of it
Ratification cannot be made so as to subject a third person to damages
A person can ratify an act even if he was not in existence or not competent when the act was done
mcq.explain: Ratification requires that the principal was in existence and competent at the time the act was done, as well as at the time of ratification; so a company cannot ratify pre-incorporation contracts. The other statements are rules in Sections 197, 199 and 200 — express or implied ratification, of the whole transaction, without harming third persons.
mcq.fast: Principal must EXIST and be COMPETENT when the act was done — so pick that option as NOT correct.

mcq.q: An agent sent goods to a distant market. They begin to perish in transit, and he cannot contact the principal, so he sells them locally. The principal is:
options: Not bound — the agent exceeded his authority
Bound only if he ratifies
Bound — the agent acted in an emergency as a person of ordinary prudence would — Section 189
Not bound, and can sue the buyer
mcq.explain: Section 189: in an emergency, an agent may do whatever a sensible person would do for his own goods to save the principal from loss. Selling perishing goods when the principal cannot be reached is a classic agency of necessity.
mcq.fast: Emergency + cannot contact principal + prudent act = principal bound.

mcq.q: A sub-agent is properly appointed by an agent. For the sub-agent's acts, the agent is responsible to the principal, and the sub-agent is responsible to:
options: The principal for all acts
No one
Third parties only
The agent, and to the principal only for fraud or wilful wrong — Section 192
mcq.explain: Under Section 192 a properly appointed sub-agent represents the principal as regards third persons. The agent is responsible to the principal for the sub-agent's acts, and the sub-agent is responsible to the agent; he is responsible to the principal only for fraud or wilful wrong.
mcq.fast: Sub-agent answers to the AGENT; to the principal only for fraud/wilful wrong.

mcq.q: In which case is an agent personally liable on a contract made on behalf of his principal?
options: When he acts for an undisclosed principal or a principal who cannot be sued
Never, in any case
Whenever the contract is in writing
Whenever the amount exceeds ₹1 lakh
mcq.explain: Section 230 presumes that an agent cannot personally enforce or be bound by contracts made for his principal. That presumption gives way, making the agent personally liable, when he acts for a foreign principal, does not disclose the principal, or acts for a named principal who cannot be sued.
mcq.fast: Agent personally liable = foreign / undisclosed / un-suable principal.

mcq.q: An agent is given authority to sell goods and recover advances he made from the proceeds. The principal dies. The agency:
options: Terminates automatically on death
Terminates if the heirs give notice
Does not terminate, as it is an agency coupled with interest — Section 202
Becomes void
mcq.explain: Under Section 202, if the agent has his own interest in the property that the agency deals with, the agency cannot be ended so as to hurt that interest, unless expressly agreed. Such an agency is not ended even by the death or insanity of the principal.
mcq.fast: Agency coupled with interest survives revocation, death and insanity.

mcq.q: An agent, without the principal's knowledge, buys the principal's goods for himself. Under Section 215 the principal may:
options: Never challenge it
Repudiate the transaction if the agent concealed material facts or dealt dishonestly
Only claim commission from the agent
Only sue for exemplary damages
mcq.explain: Section 215 provides that if an agent deals on his own account in the business of the agency without first obtaining the consent of his principal and acquainting him with all material circumstances, the principal may repudiate the transaction if a material fact was dishonestly concealed or the dealings were disadvantageous to him.
mcq.fast: Agent dealing on his own account secretly -> principal may repudiate.
